work: Rites In The Formation Of Character
heading: Liji 8 · Li Qi 禮器 · Rites In The Formation Of Character · Li Qi I.1 … Li Qi I.9

items.text: Perform the services of the ancestral temple as a natural duty.
items.quote: the services of the ancestral temple
items.conflict: Second Commandment forbids worshiping the dead; honor parents but do not pray to them.

items.text: Show them the filial duty that has come down to you.
items.quote: It was not that he was in haste to gratify his wishes; It was to show the filial duty that had come down to him.

work: Rites In The Formation Of Character
heading: Liji 8 · Li Qi 禮器 · Rites In The Formation Of Character · Li Qi II.13 … Li Qi II.21

items.text: Lead the ancestral sacrifice: bring the victim, cut out the liver, and cut up the flesh, presenting the offerings with reverence.
items.quote: The ruler himself led the victim forward... the ruler himself cut up the victim.

items.text: Assist your husband in the ancestral sacrifice: bear the dish for the liver and present the spirits as he cuts the victim.
items.quote: his wife bore the dish... his wife presented the spirits

items.text: In the ancestral temple, take your place on the east while your wife takes the west, so that together you embody the harmony of heaven and earth.
items.quote: The ruler appeared at the top of the steps on the east; his wife was in the apartment on the west... arrangements for the positions of husband and wife.

items.text: In ancestral rites, follow the head of the house as the high ministers and Great officers followed the ruler.
items.quote: The high ministers and Great officers followed the ruler; their wives followed his wife.

work: Rites In The Formation Of Character
heading: Liji 8 · Li Qi 禮器 · Rites In The Formation Of Character · Li Qi I.10 … Li Qi II.2

items.text: Do not behave as a visitor at ancestral rites; take the proper familial part.
items.quote: The relatives of a father do not put themselves into postures (like other visitors).

items.text: When sacrificing to your father, provide fitting offerings; do not be niggardly.
items.quote: An Phing-kung, in sacrificing to his father, used a sucking-pig which did not fill the dish... the superior man considered it was niggardliness.
